title: Fix the Unchecked Raw Type Usage
description: The program should store only Strings in a list and safely retrieve them.
expectedBehavior: The program should only ever store Strings in the list, so retrieving any element as a String should always succeed.
actualProblem: Using the raw type List (without a generic type parameter) disables compile-time type checking, so an Integer (42) is allowed into what was meant to be a String-only list. Casting list.get(1) to String then throws a ClassCastException at runtime.
explanation: Declaring the generic type parameter, like List<String>, lets the compiler catch attempts to insert the wrong type at compile time, preventing the ClassCastException that raw types allow to slip through to runtime.
